master.master_headline: Still acute, not imminent. The leaders' summit is the swing event; until it reports, the board holds at 8.
master.master_reasoning: This is judgment, not measurement. Same method as before: anchor on the closest civilisation-scale threats, nuclear (4.5) and great-power war (6.5), set the master farther out because those desks' midnights are lower bars than a civilisation-wide point of no return, then pull it back in because one conflict drives several threats at once and correlated risks compound. In this edition fourteen desks held, the chips desk's 10.0 is the same figure it reported last time, and the only real move was cyber, nudged from 7.0 to 6.8 on confirmed French sanctions steps and a US cold-chain warning, with effects still local. The fact-checkers also took some force out of the strongest pressure points: the Hormuz shortfall is now contested and the summit date was soft. With the Shenzhen meeting not yet reported, the honest call is to hold at 8 and keep the trend steady; steady means no net movement, not that the risks eased.

most_pressing.why: The first three-way leaders' meeting comes with no US-Russia arms treaty in force since February and the Iran standoff unresolved; US officials expect no agreement and Ukraine is not on the agenda.

most_pressing.why: About 440 kg of highly enriched uranium has not been seen by inspectors since mid-2025, and Iran was referred to the Security Council in September.

most_pressing.title: France seeks EU sanctions over the Iran-linked cold-chain attacks
most_pressing.why: An attack on about 700 French sites with at least 15 fires and blood banks hit has moved from blame to a sanctions push, and a joint US advisory calls the food cold chain a target.

most_pressing.title: A half-point Fed hike is now debated for 8-9 December
most_pressing.why: October prices rose faster than expected and the 10-year yield is above 5%, while growth stays strong and oil has fallen about 20%.

most_pressing.title: Ebola above 11,000 cases with attacks on responders
most_pressing.why: There is no licensed vaccine for this strain and most new cases are outside contact lists, though weekly growth is steady and no new exports have been seen since late October.

master.where_headed: The next days hinge on the Shenzhen leaders' meeting, the IAEA board's handling of Iran, and the COP31 close around 20 Nov. After that: Israel's coalition deadline on 6 Dec, the Fed meeting on 8 to 9 Dec with a hike priced as near-certain and its size debated, and France's push for EU sanctions within about a month. Over two years the main risks are unchanged: no arms-control successor, AI and quantum timelines running ahead of defences, and a strong El Nino meeting 2027 harvests while Gulf shipping and fertiliser stay tight. Mitigants (fusion, advanced fission, new medicine) keep advancing but arrive too late for this window.
cross_links: Iran war to Hormuz to markets: reduced Gulf shipping keeps energy and inflation pressure on, though this edition the size of the shortfall is contested and oil has fallen about 20% in a month.
Iran war to nuclear and cyber: the same conflict leaves uranium unverified and is behind the cold-chain attacks that France now wants sanctioned at EU level.
El Nino to food and climate: a near-record El Nino is already tied to drought and famine risk in Sudan and adds weight to 2027 harvest risk while fertiliser stays dearer than a year ago.
AI boom to economy, chips and energy: a giant AI listing, AI debt over $800bn flagged by a Fed official, memory shortages and a grid auction at its cap tie market risk to physical limits.
Summit to several desks: the Shenzhen meeting could ease or harden arms control, Iran and trade at once, so it is the single event most likely to move several clocks together next edition.
master.dissent: Holding could hide a slow drift closer: the cyber escalation, a hotter Fed debate and a ninth year of rule-of-law decline all point the same way, and a reader adding them could argue for 7.5. The opposite case is also live: oil down about 20%, contested Hormuz figures, steady Ebola growth and falling food prices could argue for 8.5, and any Iran de-escalation from the summit would strengthen that.

desks.name: AI Frontier & Safety
desks.midnight_definition: AI systems that can do essentially all cognitive work better, faster and cheaper than humans arrive before society has put effective steering or oversight in place (frontier threshold is the one that matters most).
desks.headline: Anthropic filing reportedly flags AI-driven R&D nearing its own threshold as IPO nears
desks.summary: Anthropic's amended S-1 says future models may soon reach its threshold for rapid AI-driven R&D progress, and METR estimates its progress pace at roughly double the earlier rate. Its Nasdaq listing is expected to price on 18 Nov and trade 19 Nov. Regulators are delaying, not tightening: the EU AI Omnibus delaying high-risk duties was adopted by Parliament and Council by July 2026.

top_stories.title: Anthropic S-1 amendment flags near-term AI-driven R&D threshold
top_stories.why_it_matters: A lab telling investors its models may soon accelerate AI research rapidly is a direct frontier-threshold signal. It reportedly delayed a pretraining run over a month to harden weight security and is weighing mandatory human sign-off on some research decisions.

top_stories.title: METR: Anthropic's R&D progress about twice the earlier pace
top_stories.why_it_matters: METR estimates about 2x (range 1.3x to 3x) versus March 2024 to October 2025, mostly from AI used in R&D; Anthropic redacted much of the most informative evidence, limiting outside checking.

top_stories.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Cyber released to vetted defenders at Critical cyber rating
top_stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI reports 48.5 percent on ExploitGym versus 32.1 percent for its prior cyber model, and an autonomous campaign reportedly reproduced 1,724 Linux vulnerabilities. Offensive-capable AI is advancing fast; figures are vendor-reported.

top_stories.why_it_matters: About 825 million shares, valuation roughly 1 to 1.4 trillion dollars, pricing 18 Nov, plus a 26B private placement. Public capital deepens the race and adds disclosure obligations.

top_stories.title: EU AI Omnibus adopted: high-risk duties pushed to Dec 2027 and Aug 2028
top_stories.why_it_matters: Standalone high-risk duties move to 2 Dec 2027, embedded ones to 2 Aug 2028; a ban on AI-generated non-consensual intimate imagery and abuse material and transparency grace periods land 2 Dec 2026.

trajectory.six_months: Listing completes and brings scrutiny of lab disclosures; more AI-accelerated R&D claims and third-party evaluations; EU 2 Dec 2026 provisions begin.
trajectory.two_years: Fast-camp forecasters expect automated coding and AI research by 2027 to 2028; slower ones see broad cognitive automation in the 2030s; oversight likely lags either way.

desks.name: Biosecurity & Pandemics
desks.midnight_definition: A pandemic or biological event worse than COVID-19 in global deaths and disruption.
desks.headline: Ebola tops 11,000 cases amid attacks on responders; US measles status reported lost
desks.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in DRC is the largest in the country's history, with 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 deaths as of 11 Nov, no approved vaccine, and conflict repeatedly halting response work. Export has been limited so far (Uganda declared over, Kenya and Nigeria quiet since late October). The US measles elimination status loss was reported on 14 to 16 November, and H5N1 keeps producing sporadic US human cases. The outcome of the 2 to 13 Nov pathogen-sharing treaty round was not found.

top_stories.title: Ebola in DR Congo passes 11,000 confirmed cases; response hit by attacks
top_stories.why_it_matters: Official institute figures show 11,042 cases and 5,387 deaths across eight provinces; youths burned an Ebola treatment facility in Ituri and militia clashes paused work in one area. Ervebo is entering a trial to test cross-protection against Bundibugyo.

top_stories.title: Africa CDC: Ebola in DRC still not under control after six months
top_stories.why_it_matters: Africa CDC says most new cases are not on contact lists, while WHO sees slowing in some early hotspots, so the signals are mixed.

top_stories.title: UKHSA: Ebola exports contained for now; 72 US human H5 cases since 2024
top_stories.why_it_matters: As of 1 Nov, DRC had 10,532 confirmed cases (up 472 in a week) with 84% contact tracing; Kenya has 9 cases and none since 19 Oct, Nigeria 1 imported case with no spread. The US has 72 confirmed H5 human cases since 2024, 42 linked to dairy cattle.

top_stories.title: US has lost measles elimination status, health authorities say
top_stories.why_it_matters: A US administration official confirmed the revocation after 26 years; experts say regaining it requires more vaccination and better surveillance. A PAHO page confirming this was not seen.

top_stories.title: Washington State reports first US bird flu death of 2026
top_stories.why_it_matters: Fatal H5N1 case in Yakima County with dairy cattle exposure; officials rate public risk as low and no person-to-person spread was reported.

top_stories.title: Ninth round of pandemic agreement pathogen-sharing talks set for 2-13 Nov
top_stories.why_it_matters: The PABS annex is still unfinished after repeated missed targets, so the pandemic treaty cannot open for signature. Outcome of the round not found.

trajectory.six_months: Ebola likely continues at high levels in DRC given insecurity and untraced cases, with vaccine cross-protection trial data possible in early 2027. US measles likely rises into spring; H5N1 cases stay sporadic.
trajectory.two_years: Outcome hinges on whether the PABS annex is agreed and surveillance and vaccination capacity recover. A COVID-scale event remains a tail risk rather than a baseline.

desks.name: Biotech, Longevity & BCI
desks.midnight_definition: The first therapy shown in humans to slow or reverse biological ageing broadly, not just one disease.
desks.headline: Moderna races to file personalised melanoma vaccine; no broad anti-ageing proof yet
desks.summary: Narrow-front medicine keeps advancing: Moderna's chief executive says he and Merck are racing to file their personalised mRNA melanoma vaccine with the FDA and expects approval in 2027, and gene therapy approvals continue for rare diseases. None of this is a therapy that slows ageing broadly, and the searches for human ageing-endpoint trials found nothing new.

desks.name: Semiconductors & Quantum
desks.midnight_definition: A fault-tolerant quantum computer performs commercially or cryptographically relevant work (e.g. breaking RSA/elliptic-curve keys) that classical machines cannot.
desks.headline: US tightens AI chip export rules as memory shortage persists and quantum waits on proof
desks.summary: On 16 Nov the US issued an interim rule requiring licences for advanced AI chips going to five countries' data centres and closing remote access for China-headquartered firms. DRAM price gains are slowing but still positive (about 20% in 4Q26). Quantum vendors still target 2029 fault tolerance with no independent proof, and I found no new quantum milestone this edition.

top_stories.title: US tightens AI chip export rule: SE Asia licences, remote-access loophole shut
top_stories.why_it_matters: Commerce's BIS interim final rule requires licences for advanced AI chip exports to data centres in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil, and for giving China-headquartered firms remote access; existing arrangements get 90 days.

top_stories.title: TrendForce: DRAM contract prices to rise ~20% in 4Q26, slower than 2Q/3Q
top_stories.why_it_matters: Price gains are decelerating from about 80% (2Q26) and 40% (3Q26) but remain positive; HBM stack choices for Rubin Ultra could shift 2027 pricing.

top_stories.title: Microsoft shows Majorana 2 chip, targets fault tolerance by 2029
top_stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft claims long qubit lifetimes and a 2029 target for a practical machine, but the paper is not yet peer reviewed and working error correction is unproven. Quantinuum also raised about $1.68B in a US IPO the same period, a sign of investor confidence.

top_stories.title: Neutral-atom and ion firms push logical-qubit counts and funding
top_stories.why_it_matters: Infleqtion entangled 30 logical qubits and targets 100 by 2028; Atom Computing's Magne project aims for 50 logical qubits by late 2026; Germany committed up to EUR 640M to quantum competitions. Progress is broad but still far short of crypto-breaking scale.

top_stories.title: Analysts expect HBM prices up 50%+ in 2027; Nvidia servers reportedly dearer
top_stories.why_it_matters: Reports say Nvidia may raise Vera Rubin and Grace Blackwell server prices over 15% in early 2027, and some DDR5 prices have nearly quadrupled in a year. Memory, not just logic, is now an AI bottleneck.

top_stories.title: Quantinuum claims 99.9995% logical fidelity on Helios
top_stories.why_it_matters: Carried from edition 001: roughly a tenfold logical error drop, company claim, not independently verified.

trajectory.six_months: More logical-qubit announcements (Atom/Microsoft 50-logical-qubit target by end of 2026, Quantinuum and IBM updates) and DARPA testing of Majorana 2. Memory remains tight and contract prices stay elevated.
trajectory.two_years: Logical qubits likely reach the low hundreds with better error rates; 2029 vendor targets will be tested by then. HBM and DRAM supply may ease only as new capacity and advanced nodes arrive after 2027.

desks.name: Climate & Earth Systems
desks.midnight_definition: Crossing self-reinforcing tipping points (ice sheets, AMOC, Amazon, coral reefs, permafrost) that lock in severe warming regardless of later action.
desks.headline: COP31 enters final days with fossil-exit wording unresolved as El Nino nears record
desks.summary: COP31 in Antalya (9-20 Nov) is in its ministerial final stretch; the 16 Nov draft cover decision calls for accelerated fossil-fuel phase-out and expresses deep concern about breaching 1.5C, but the Arab Group and others resist top-down targets and finance is unresolved. Separately, a very strong El Nino is approaching record strength, raising odds of record global heat in 2027. No newer physical evidence on tipping elements was found.

top_stories.title: COP31 draft urges accelerated fossil-fuel phase-out; presidency says not final
top_stories.why_it_matters: The draft also backs a 35% electricity-share goal by 2035 and voices deep concern over 1.5C; the negotiations president warned parties will not all agree, so language may be diluted.

top_stories.title: COP31 final week: finance, fossil fuels, electrification, just transition still open
top_stories.why_it_matters: Developing countries want firmer public adaptation money; developed countries favour private finance; the Arab Group rejects imposed global targets. Scheduled close is 20 Nov.

top_stories.title: El Nino heads toward record: Aug-Oct relative index near +2.0C
top_stories.why_it_matters: Relative Nino 3.4 index is about 0.1C behind 1997-98 for the season; NOAA's October outlook gave 70% for a historic Nov-Jan event, a strong driver of 2027 record heat and coral and weather stress.

top_stories.title: Pledged public climate finance from big donors about 70% below 2025
top_stories.why_it_matters: Aid cuts shrink adaptation money as disputes over developed-country obligations deepen.

top_stories.title: UNEP: 1.5C overshoot now inevitable; policies point to about 2.8C by 2100
top_stories.why_it_matters: Emissions are far above a no-overshoot path; returning below 1.5C would need large carbon removal.

top_stories.title: October 2026 warmest on record; 2026 virtually certain to top 1.5C
top_stories.why_it_matters: Record-strength El Nino building makes 2027 records likely.

trajectory.six_months: COP31 probably closes with a compromise cover decision, possibly after overrunning; El Nino peaks around the turn of the year and monthly temperature records are likely into early 2027.
trajectory.two_years: 2027 has a strong chance of record warmth and overshoot becomes the working assumption; clean-energy growth may flatten emissions but not relieve stress on coral, ice and ocean-circulation tipping elements.

signals_to_watch: COP31 final cover decision (scheduled 20 Nov 2026, possible overrun): does fossil phase-out language survive?
Fate of the 35%-electricity-by-2035 goal and adaptation finance (tripling to 120bn USD sought by developing countries)
Next NOAA ENSO update (December) and Nino 3.4 peak Nov 2026 to Jan 2027
Next Copernicus monthly bulletin (early Dec) and 2026 annual ranking (Jan 2027)
desks.clock_reasoning: No new evidence on tipping-element timing, and COP31 remains unresolved, so the clock holds. The near-record El Nino adds near-term heat risk but is a cyclical driver, not a tipping event. This is judgment, not measurement; someone weighting tipping-point science as more imminent could place it under 5.

Extreme weather events of the last 90 days
desks.bottom_line: Treat 1.5C overshoot and a record-warm 2027 as the planning baseline; watch the 20 Nov COP31 text for whether any fossil-exit language survives.
desks.why_it_matters: Weak or diluted outcomes and falling climate finance leave vulnerable and low-income countries more exposed to a record El Nino year and continued warming.
desks.confidence_basis: Medium: official draft coverage and ENSO indices agree across sources, but the latest days and primary NOAA data were not retrieved and tipping-point evidence was not refreshed.
would_change: Closer: new peer-reviewed evidence of AMOC or ice-sheet destabilisation, or COP31 collapse without a text
Farther: COP31 deal with binding fossil-exit language and funded adaptation

decision_points.what: Scheduled close of COP31 in Antalya (overrun possible)
Approximate: next Copernicus monthly climate bulletin (date unconfirmed)

affects.why: Record heat and El Nino disrupt agriculture, insurance and energy demand.
Finance and fossil-fuel splits strain North-South and producer-consumer relations.
The 35% electrification goal and fossil language shape energy transition policy.

desks.since_last: Added the 16 Nov draft details (accelerated phase-out wording, 120bn adaptation ask) and near-record El Nino readings; no 17-18 Nov news found, no physical-evidence change, so the clock holds.

notes: Daily Sabah 16 Nov confirms draft wording on accelerated phase-out, 35% electricity share by 2035, deep concern about 1.5C, adaptation ask of at least $120bn, Bowen saying not final, close on Friday 20 Nov.
News of Bahrain confirms 9-20 Nov dates, Arab Group rejecting imposed targets, 23% to 35% electricity share, finance split; it does not mention $120bn (Daily Sabah does).

The Watchers 10 Nov confirms RONI +2.0 (table +1.97) for Aug-Oct, 0.10C behind 1997-98, weekly traditional Nino 3.4 +3.3C (week of 4 Nov). NOAA 70% is for a Nov-Jan RONI of at least +2.5C, a slightly different framing from 'historic event'.
Copernicus and Carbon Brief fetches were blocked, so stories 3-5 are not checked. Clock held at 8.5, judgment fairly flagged.

desks.name: Cyber & Critical Infrastructure
desks.midnight_definition: A cyberattack or cascading failure takes down critical infrastructure across a major country for weeks.
desks.headline: France seeks EU Iran sanctions over fridge attacks; US warns cold chain is a target
desks.summary: France's foreign minister said on 16 Nov that Paris will present evidence to EU ministers and seek a sanctions list within a month over the October campaign that hit about 700 French commercial sites and caused at least 15 fires. A joint US FBI/CISA/HHS/USDA/DOT advisory on 5 Nov confirms the technique is a worldwide threat, and a second wave reached over 115 stores in six European countries, with blood storage sites touched. Iran-linked PLC attacks on US water and energy are also ongoing. All effects remain local and recover in days.

top_stories.title: France to seek EU sanctions on Iran over fridge cyberattacks; 15 fires
top_stories.why_it_matters: A cyber campaign with physical effects is becoming a formal EU sanctions matter. Iran's UN mission did not respond in the coverage seen; Tehran routinely denies such operations.

top_stories.title: FBI, CISA and three agencies warn of attacks on refrigeration controllers
top_stories.why_it_matters: The US government says attackers are exploiting internet-exposed temperature controllers worldwide to force heating or defrost cycles. Sectors at risk include grocery, healthcare, chemicals and transport; the advisory names no actor.

top_stories.title: Iran-affiliated actors keep exploiting PLCs; US advisory expanded to Siemens, Schneider
top_stories.why_it_matters: CISA, FBI and EPA say water, energy and local government operators suffered disruption and financial loss. The page showed no publication date for the update, so month is approximate.

top_stories.title: Cold-chain attack timeline: 13-country second wave, UK meat suppliers, Pentagon probe
top_stories.why_it_matters: An analyst timeline lists a 2 Nov second wave across 13 countries and a suspected cyber cause for August US commissary freezer failures. Counts differ from the US advisory (115 stores, six countries); some claims are unproven.

top_stories.title: FBI: Salt Typhoon still ongoing, reaching beyond telecoms, 80+ countries
top_stories.why_it_matters: An FBI official says the Chinese espionage campaign continues and has affected over 80 countries (his estimate). It is espionage, not disruption, but implies prepositioned access in telecoms.

top_stories.title: Coordinated attack on about 30 Minnesota water systems; boil notices
top_stories.why_it_matters: Internet-facing PLCs were hit in about six states; no contamination reported and attribution was not formally determined. It is the template for the water-sector risk the November advisory update addresses.

trajectory.six_months: Expect an EU sanctions listing on Iranian IRGC-linked persons, more exploitation of exposed cold-chain and PLC devices, and copycat or retaliatory activity. Most incidents stay local and last days.
trajectory.two_years: A large pool of poorly secured operational technology, AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and normalised state retaliation raise the odds of a multi-sector event, though hardening mandates (US advisories, UK bill) could blunt it.

signals_to_watch: EU foreign ministers' handling of France's evidence and any sanctions list (France said within about a month)
Formal US or UK attribution of the water, commissary or UK power incidents
Any attack on a large utility or grid operator rather than small operators
UK Cyber Security and Resilience Bill: remaining Lords third reading and Commons consideration of amendments
Further FBI/CISA advisories on OT devices
desks.clock_reasoning: A state-attributed campaign with fires, blood-storage exposure and a joint US warning argues slightly closer, so I move from 7.0 to 6.8. Still, every observed effect is local and recovered in days; nothing approaches a weeks-long outage across a major country. A resilience-minded reader could argue for 8; an AI-offence-focused one for 5.

desks.bottom_line: Operators of refrigeration and water controllers should pull them off the public internet now; expect EU-Iran sanctions escalation within weeks.
desks.why_it_matters: Food retailers, cold storage, hospitals and blood services, and small water utilities face physical consequences from weakly secured controllers, and a state-attribution fight raises escalation risk with Iran.
desks.confidence_basis: Official statements relayed by press and a US joint advisory agree on the campaign, but counts differ and I reached no primary government pages.
would_change: Closer: a successful attack on a grid operator or large water utility causing multi-day regional outage
Closer: new US/EU findings of destructive access across many sectors

decision_points.what: Approximate end of the one-month window France gave for an EU sanctions list
Soft marker: EU foreign ministers' consideration of French evidence (date not confirmed)

affects.why: Attribution to the IRGC and EU sanctions feed Iran war escalation and Europe-Iran relations.
Iran-linked PLC attacks hit energy and water operators.
Food spoilage, fires and blood storage exposure hit the public directly.

desks.since_last: France moved from attribution to concrete sanctions steps on 16 Nov, and a 5 Nov US joint advisory and fire count (15) add severity, so the clock moves slightly closer to 6.8. No incident exceeded local scale.
desks.calibration_note: Changed from 7.0, accepting the desk's small move. The fact-checker confirmed France moving from blame to seeking EU sanctions within a month, at least 15 fires and blood banks hit, plus a joint US warning that the cold chain is a target. Effects are still local and short, so a fifth of a minute only.

notes: Clock moved 7.0 to 6.8. desks.name: Global Economy & SPY
desks.midnight_definition: THREAT lens: a systemic financial crisis on the scale of 2008 or worse (disorderly bond/credit/bank failure with a deep equity collapse and a frozen financial system).
desks.headline: Fed 50bp hike now debated for Dec 8-9 as 10-yr holds above 5% and oil eases
desks.summary: Bond markets are pricing a hawkish Fed: the 10-year Treasury yield is above 5%, the 2-year jumped sharply after a hot October CPI, and a Fed governor has floated a half-point hike in December. Growth and jobs are firm (Q3 GDP 3.4% annualised, unemployment 4.1%) and oil has fallen about 20% in a month, but stocks near records lean on AI earnings while Fed officials flag AI-linked debt above $800B. No bank or credit failure was found.

top_stories.title: Fed's Waller says a 50bp December hike should be considered after hot CPI
top_stories.why_it_matters: A voting governor openly backing a larger move raised the odds of a jumbo hike; the 10-year rose 14bp to 5.00% and the 2-year 19bp to 4.738% that day. CME pricing that day still favoured 25bp (90.5%) over 50bp (9.5%).

top_stories.title: October CPI +0.4% m/m, above the 0.3% expected
top_stories.why_it_matters: A third straight upside surprise in prices; shelter rose 0.3% and energy 0.7%. No annual October rate was published because of the earlier shutdown data gap; September's annual rate was 3.7%.

top_stories.title: Bond yields top 5.13% while equities lag in pricing further hikes
top_stories.why_it_matters: Futures priced three quarter-point hikes through March (to 4.50-4.75%), while strategists warn stocks are not positioned for a longer cycle. A Fed governor flagged AI-related debt above $800B this year.

top_stories.title: Weekly review: 2-year yield surge, 50bp hike priced, Fed speakers, minutes due
top_stories.why_it_matters: Describes a roughly 35bp weekly rise in the 2-year yield, rate futures pricing a possible half-point December hike, GDP up 3.4% in Q3, oil down about 20% in a month, and public friction between the Treasury Secretary and the Fed over hiking.

trajectory.six_months: Base case is one to three more Fed hikes, long yields in a 4.5-5.5% range and choppy tech-led equities; lower oil could ease inflation, while a further hot print or AI-credit event would deepen stress.
trajectory.two_years: Record interest costs, AI capex debt, leveraged nonbank finance and bank bond losses could end in a soft landing with rotation away from AI leaders, or a disorderly deleveraging; analysts disagree widely.

signals_to_watch: Minutes of the last FOMC meeting (due week of Nov 16) and the Dec 8-9 decision: 25bp vs 50bp
November CPI on Dec 10, day after the Fed decision
10-year yield sustained above 5.3% (Oct 5 closing high 5.31%) or weak Treasury auctions
S&P 500 drawdown past 10% from its record, VIX above 30, or any AI-linked credit default
Oil path and Iran war developments

Held at 7.8: new evidence cuts both ways, with hike size debate and a 2-year surge pushing closer, but strong GDP, 4.1% unemployment, oil down 20% and well-capitalised banks pushing farther. Judgment, not measurement; a more worried reader would weight bond-equity divergence, a calmer one the strong growth data.

desks.bottom_line: Expect a Dec 8-9 Fed hike of at least 25bp with real odds of 50bp; long yields above 5% are the pressure point to watch.
desks.why_it_matters: Higher-for-longer rates hit equity valuations, bank bond portfolios, leveraged funds and AI-related borrowers, and raise borrowing costs for governments, firms and households.
desks.confidence_basis: Rests on dated secondary press accounts of Fed and CPI events; direct market-data pages were blocked and S&P levels conflict.

Farther: soft CPI on Dec 10, yields falling below 4.8%, continued oil decline

desks.name: Energy & Fusion
desks.midnight_definition: The first fusion plant delivers net electricity to a grid commercially, so energy abundance becomes a build-out problem rather than a physics problem.
desks.headline: Fusion still pre-net-energy while PJM hits its price cap short on reserves
desks.summary: No device has yet shown net electricity; funding is at record levels (IAEA counts about $22B raised) and CFS and Helion machines are targeted for 2027-2028. On the grid side, the PJM 2028/29 auction cleared at its cap and about 6.8 GW short of its reliability target, and IEA projects global demand growth of about 3.6% a year to 2030 with data centres a major driver. Advanced fission is moving faster, with a Natrium construction permit issued in March 2026.

top_stories.title: IAEA World Fusion Outlook: 26 plants planned, $22B raised so far
top_stories.why_it_matters: The most authoritative fresh snapshot: record funding, 174 facilities worldwide, and most planned power plants aiming for the 2030s. It estimates a further $80B of private capital is needed.

top_stories.title: PJM 2028/29 capacity auction hits price cap, 6.8 GW short of target
top_stories.why_it_matters: Shows data-centre load growth outrunning new supply in the largest US grid: the auction cleared at the cap, drew only about 525 MW of new resources, and fell short of the reserve target for a second time.

top_stories.title: IEA: global power demand to grow about 3.6% a year to 2030
top_stories.why_it_matters: The IEA's Electricity 2026 outlook expects demand to reach roughly 33,600 TWh by 2030, with US data centres accounting for about half of US demand growth.

top_stories.title: NRC issues first Natrium construction permit for Wyoming plant
top_stories.why_it_matters: First US construction permit for a commercial-scale non-light-water reactor in about four decades, issued in roughly 18 months; operation targeted around 2030 pending a separate operating licence.

top_stories.title: PJM market monitor: Q1 wholesale power cost up 76% on data-centre load
top_stories.why_it_matters: Wholesale cost reached $136.53/MWh versus $77.78 a year earlier; capacity costs rose 398%. The monitor urged data centres to bring their own generation; PJM says markets are working as designed.

top_stories.title: PJM-commissioned review: data-centre demand ~30 GW by 2030, ~11.5 GW supply gap
top_stories.why_it_matters: Latest PJM-sponsored forecast review sees data-centre load reaching about 82 GW by 2047 and a possible 11.5 GW reliability shortfall by 2030 without faster supply; 294 local moratoriums were passed Jan-Jul 2026.

trajectory.six_months: Expect continued fundraising, SPARC assembly and commissioning news, and Helion Orion construction updates; no net-electricity fusion result is likely. Data-centre-driven grid strain and power-price politics will keep growing.
trajectory.two_years: SPARC may have first plasma and early physics results (target 2027), and Helion will have shown whether its 2028 date is realistic. Grid-connected fusion electricity is still unlikely by end-2028; the 2030s remain the central estimate.

signals_to_watch: SPARC first plasma (CFS target 2027) and any slip in that date
Helion Orion construction progress and the 2028 Microsoft 50 MW delivery date
US appropriations for DOE's new Office of Fusion and the milestone programme
Fusion Industry Association annual funding figures (next mid-2027) versus the record $4.48B
PJM and other grid operators' capacity auctions as data-centre demand grows
desks.clock_reasoning: No fusion plant has shown net electricity, and credible plans cluster in the 2030s, with Helion's 2028 date viewed sceptically. A day after edition 001 nothing found justifies moving the clock; the grid-strain evidence (PJM cap, IEA demand outlook) is context rather than the fusion threshold. Bullish on Helion would go under 10; weighting historical slippage would go above 20.

Storage/solar statistics and last-48-hour news not covered
desks.since_last: Same day as edition 002; added PJM load-forecast review (2 Nov) and market-monitor price data; no fusion milestone news found, so the clock holds at 13.0.

decision_points.what: Approx. Fusion Industry Association annual funding report (mid-2027, date unconfirmed)
CFS target window for SPARC first plasma (2027)

affects.why: Data-centre load is the main driver of grid strain and price rises.
Higher wholesale power costs feed electricity inflation.

desks.bottom_line: Fusion net electricity is still years away, with the 2030s the central estimate; watch SPARC and Helion milestones and plan for grid strain in the meantime.
desks.why_it_matters: Data-centre demand is straining grids and lifting power prices now, while fusion relief sits beyond this decade; households, utilities and AI builders are all affected.
desks.calibration_note: Kept. No fusion net-electricity milestone; grid strain (PJM at its price cap, short on reserves) is confirmed context, not the threshold.

desks.name: War & Geopolitics
desks.midnight_definition: Direct, sustained armed conflict between major powers (for example US-China, US-Russia or NATO-Russia), with the potential for nuclear escalation.
desks.headline: Xi, Trump, Putin to meet at APEC in Shenzhen; no arms treaty, Hormuz traffic sharply down
desks.summary: The first three-way meeting of the US, Chinese and Russian presidents is expected on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen (18-19 November); New START lapsed in February and Washington wants a new treaty including China, which says that is unrealistic for now. The US-Iran war is deadlocked, with US strikes on Qeshm and Hormuz and ship attacks continuing into early November while Qatar mediates. In Ukraine, Russia is hardening its terms and concentrating attacks around Kostyantynivka and Dobropillya.

top_stories.title: Xi, Trump and Putin to meet in Shenzhen; arms control and Iran on the agenda
top_stories.why_it_matters: The White House says proliferation is a focus; New START expired in February and no replacement exists. A senior US official reportedly expects no agreement, and Ukraine is not expected to be raised.

top_stories.title: Qeshm and Hormuz hit again as mediators try to stop US-Iran escalation
top_stories.why_it_matters: UKMTO counted at least 11 ships attacked in the week to 6 November, three sunk, and transits about 65% below pre-war. The IRGC said its missile-range limit no longer applies, raising the stakes of any renewed war.

top_stories.title: ISW: Russia hardens demands as US floats NATO-for-Donbas idea
top_stories.why_it_matters: Reported US proposal of NATO membership for Ukraine in return for leaving Donbas clashes with Russia's aims; Zelensky said he would put such terms to a referendum. Russia is massing on the Dobropillya-Kostyantynivka sector.
top_stories.source_name: Institute for the Study of War / Critical Threats

top_stories.title: US strikes Iranian site on Qeshm; Iran says Hormuz plan reply unconvincing
top_stories.why_it_matters: Sharpest US-Iran exchange of fire of the period; Iran insists all seven of its conditions be met before reopening Hormuz.

top_stories.title: Ukraine war stagnates; Kyiv claims record daily Russian losses
top_stories.why_it_matters: No settlement in sight; casualty claims are Ukraine's and unverified.

top_stories.title: APEC opens in Shenzhen with Xi as host
top_stories.why_it_matters: Xi hosts APEC in Shenzhen, where the trilateral with Trump and Putin is expected on the sidelines; Ukraine is not on the agenda.

trajectory.six_months: Renewed major US-Iran combat is a live risk after the US midterms, per US officials cited by Israeli and Qatari-linked reporting, unless a phased Hormuz-for-blockade deal lands. Ukraine remains high-intensity with talks over territory and security guarantees unresolved.
trajectory.two_years: Without a successor to New START and with three simultaneous theaters, risk of miscalculation among nuclear powers stays elevated; outcomes range from frozen conflicts to a Taiwan or NATO-flank crisis.

desks.bottom_line: Treat the Shenzhen meeting (APEC, 18-19 November) as the near-term hinge: absent an arms-control or Hormuz breakthrough, assume continued three-theater risk.

desks.name: Governance & Information
desks.midnight_definition: A breakdown of the shared ability to govern and to agree on facts, such that large societies can no longer correct their own mistakes.
desks.headline: Rule-of-law decline hits ninth year; Brazil and Israel votes settled inside institutions
desks.summary: The World Justice Project's 2026 index reports rule-of-law scores falling in 62% of 143 countries, the ninth straight year of net decline, adding to V-Dem, Freedom House and RSF lows, while the EIU shows a small global uptick. Brazil's electoral court confirmed Lula's win and the runner-up withdrew his annulment request, shifting to a narrower legal case. Israel's post-election coalition talks are open, with a 6 December mandate deadline.

top_stories.title: Brazil: electoral court confirms Lula win; Flavio Bolsonaro drops annulment bid
top_stories.why_it_matters: The court said extended voting hours did not change the tally and rejected a claim about party observers. The source is affiliated with the winner's party, so framing may differ elsewhere.

top_stories.why_it_matters: After the 27 October election the seat split is 48 for Eisenkot's bloc, 53 for Netanyahu's bloc and 19 for two Palestinian-led factions. Disputes over rotation of the premiership and conscription exemptions are the main obstacles, and repeat elections remain possible.

top_stories.title: UN approves rule change so budget credits are returned only against cash received
top_stories.why_it_matters: Targets the UN's cash shortage; the controller estimates 1.1 billion dollars less is returned to member states over the next year. The 2027 budget decision is still pending.

top_stories.title: US midterms: Democrats win both chambers, per NPR tally of AP calls
top_stories.why_it_matters: A change of party control through the normal count, with no vote-count disputes reported in the article. Mid-decade redistricting stays contested between the parties.

top_stories.title: Record 313 internet shutdowns across 52 countries in 2025
top_stories.why_it_matters: Access Now counts the most deliberate shutdowns it has recorded; they cut off news and the ability to verify events.

trajectory.six_months: Expect an Israeli government or a path to new elections by late December, rulings on Brazil's abuse-of-power case, and the 2027 V-Dem, Freedom House and RSF editions (March to May) showing whether erosion continues.
trajectory.two_years: The 2028 US cycle, AI-generated content at scale and UN funding limits are the main stressors; the question is whether courts and election bodies keep absorbing disputed outcomes.

desks.name: Nuclear & Strategic Weapons
desks.midnight_definition: The first use of a nuclear weapon in war, or an uncontrolled escalation toward large-scale nuclear exchange, which cannot be undone.
desks.headline: Iran's uranium still unlocated as IAEA board meets; no US-Russia limits since February
desks.summary: No treaty has capped US and Russian strategic arsenals since New START lapsed in February 2026, and the Bulletin's Doomsday Clock stands at a record 85 seconds. The IAEA board already found Iran in noncompliance and referred it to the UN Security Council on 9 September (23-3), where Russian and Chinese vetoes make action unlikely; inspectors have not located Iran's roughly 440 kg of near-weapons-grade uranium, and Iranian clerics are debating dropping the no-bomb pledge. North Korea is expanding enrichment and Russia-NATO nuclear signalling continues at a steady level.

top_stories.title: IAEA says Iran's highly enriched uranium still unaccounted for; board meets next
top_stories.why_it_matters: Inspectors have been shut out since the June 2025 strikes and cannot say where about 440 kg of near-weapons-grade uranium is; Iran rules out regular monitoring for now.

top_stories.title: IAEA board votes 23-3 to report Iran to the UN Security Council
top_stories.why_it_matters: Second formal noncompliance step after June; Russia, China and Niger opposed, so Security Council sanctions look unlikely, while Iran ties access to a wider deal and talks remain stalled.

top_stories.title: IAEA reports a second North Korean uranium enrichment building at Yongbyon
top_stories.why_it_matters: A new building could hold up to 28 centrifuge cascades alongside Kangson; fissile output grows with no inspectors in the country since 2009.

top_stories.why_it_matters: The last cap on deployed strategic warheads lapsed; the US wants a broader deal including China.

trajectory.six_months: Expect no binding US-Russia limits, an IAEA-Iran standoff with a stalled Security Council track, and further North Korean fissile-material growth. An explosive test by any state is possible but not the base case.
trajectory.two_years: Without a successor framework, warhead uploads and a three-way US-Russia-China build-up become the default. Iran's nuclear choice and the testing moratorium are the main wildcards.

desks.why_it_matters: Without caps or inspections, the US, Russia, China and the Middle East face higher miscalculation and proliferation risk, with Iran's unlocated stockpile the sharpest near-term gap.

desks.name: Food, Water & Resources
desks.midnight_definition: Simultaneous failure of several major food-producing regions, or a resource shock, that causes mass hunger across multiple continents.
desks.headline: Hormuz shipping still disrupted while a strong El Niño builds toward the 2027 harvests
desks.summary: Hormuz traffic is reported to remain well below pre-war levels with tanker attacks into mid-November, though the size of the shortfall is contested, and NOAA reports a strong El Nino with high odds of staying strong into early 2027. Fertiliser costs are 3-17% above last year in the US and Sudan already shows El Nino drought feeding famine risk, but headline food prices are mild (FAO 133.9) and grain stocks are near record.

top_stories.title: Hormuz shipping reported about 65% below pre-war; two more tankers reported hit 16 Nov
top_stories.why_it_matters: UKMTO logged eight incidents in its latest week, seven on tankers. IEA says Gulf oil exports reached 18.4 mb/d in October, still 26% under pre-war, with a projected Q4 supply surplus of 1.7 mb/d. These figures could not be independently checked this edition, and other reports put Gulf exports near pre-war levels.

top_stories.title: NOAA: strong El Nino in place, over 79% odds it stays strong into early 2027
top_stories.why_it_matters: Niño 3.4 anomaly near +2.5C and a roughly 60% chance of historic strength raise risks for crops in Australia, India, Southeast Asia and Brazil. Next update is 10 December.

top_stories.title: FAO food price index confirmed: 133.9 in October, down 1.2%, still 5.9% up on year
top_stories.why_it_matters: Confirmed on FAO's own page: cereals fell 4.5% and sugar rose 6.6%, vegetable oils stay very high at 199.2. Prices are lagging the fertiliser and weather shocks.

top_stories.title: Red Sea recovery continues: Suez transits at post-crisis high, no attacks since August
top_stories.why_it_matters: Suez October transits were about 34% below pre-crisis and Bab el Mandeb about 46% below, but both are rising. A large unexplained blast near Bab el Mandeb on 6 November keeps the risk live.

top_stories.title: Sudan IPC alert: famine risk grows in Darfur and Kordofan as El Nino drought hits half the country
top_stories.why_it_matters: The first sign of El Nino damaging a food-crisis country: drought across roughly half of Sudan, rising prices and scarce clean water, with WHO's appeal only 23% funded.

top_stories.title: US retail fertiliser: all eight products dearer than a year ago, anhydrous +17%
top_stories.why_it_matters: DTN's first-week-November survey shows urea at $662/ton (+11% on year) and anhydrous at $1,003 (+17%), month-on-month mixed with no move of 5% or more. Input costs stay high going into 2027 planting.

trajectory.six_months: Fertiliser cost and availability will shape 2027 planting just as El Niño impacts on Southern Hemisphere and Asian crops emerge. Sudan and other hotspots likely worsen without funding.
trajectory.two_years: If Hormuz stays impaired and El Niño cuts yields in several regions, a multi-continent food price spike is plausible; if shipping normalises, the system probably absorbs it with regional hunger increases.

desks.name: Robotics & Autonomy
desks.midnight_definition: General-purpose robots (humanoid or otherwise) doing ordinary physical work at scale more cheaply than human labour, across many job types rather than in a few controlled niches.
desks.headline: Autonomy keeps spreading city by city; humanoids still fail fine tasks
desks.summary: Narrow autonomy keeps scaling: Tesla opened unsupervised robotaxis in San Antonio on 9 Nov (its eighth market), Zoox is adding cities, and Aurora has passed 500,000 driverless truck miles. Capital is flowing to humanoid makers (Unitree listed in Shanghai in August at roughly 9 billion dollars), but published robot-model results on fine manipulation remain weak and humanoid output is small.

top_stories.why_it_matters: Tesla now lists eight unsupervised markets (Austin, Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth, San Antonio, Miami, Orlando, Tampa) but discloses no fleet size; trackers saw only a handful of cars in San Antonio on day one, and whether safety monitors ride along is unclear.

top_stories.why_it_matters: One model drives a humanoid's legs and hands, but reported success was 92% for unscrewing a bulb and about 40% for sealing a bag, so dexterity is unsolved.

desks.name: Global Health & Demographics
desks.midnight_definition: Demographic and social strain (ageing, shrinking workforces, health-funding collapse) becomes so severe that major societies can no longer sustain their pensions, health systems and workforce.
desks.headline: Aid cuts bite: Global Fund at $12.6B, 13.5M children still unvaccinated
desks.summary: Health financing keeps shrinking: the Global Fund closed its eighth replenishment at $12.64 billion, and 2025 aid fell a record 23%. The July 2026 WHO/UNICEF immunisation estimates show a small improvement in 2025 (13.5 million zero-dose children, 745,000 fewer than 2024) but still above 2019, with the full effect of the cuts not yet visible. On the demographic side, South Korea's births are rebounding for a 26th straight month, a counter-current to the usual decline story.

top_stories.title: Zero-dose children fall to 13.5 million in 2025, still above 2019
top_stories.why_it_matters: WHO/UNICEF estimates show a slight improvement over 2024 but 74 countries are worse than in 2019 and the world is 3.9 million above its 2025 milestone. Measles coverage has not recovered, with 1.8 million more unprotected children than in 2019.

top_stories.title: Global Fund board welcomes final $12.64B eighth replenishment
top_stories.why_it_matters: The total is US$12.64 billion; $10.78 billion is allocated to countries for 2026-2028 plus $260 million for catalytic investments, and the Fund is pushing faster transition of countries to self-reliance. HIV, TB and malaria programmes face tighter budgets.

top_stories.title: South Korea births up 13% in August, 26th straight monthly rise
top_stories.why_it_matters: About 23,700 births in August; January-August births are up 14.5% and the monthly fertility rate reached 0.87. Still far below replacement, but it shows demographic decline is not uniform.

top_stories.title: Global aid fell 23.1% in 2025, the biggest drop on record
top_stories.why_it_matters: Preliminary OECD data show the US drove roughly three-quarters of the fall and humanitarian aid fell about 36%, the funding backdrop for all global health programmes.

trajectory.six_months: Expect early 2027 birth counts from East Asia and first hard data on how aid cuts affect HIV, TB and malaria programmes as 2026-2028 Global Fund allocations take effect.
trajectory.two_years: Further donor retrenchment would likely reverse immunisation gains in fragile settings, while ageing keeps forcing pension and retirement-age fights in Europe and Asia.

Korea monthly births (Statistics Korea, early each month) and 2026 annual total in Feb 2027

desks.name: Space
desks.midnight_definition: Permanent human presence beyond Earth becomes self-sustaining in practice: routine, cheap, fully reusable heavy lift plus a crewed base that persists.
desks.headline: Flight 15 ship catch reported; refuelling, Mengzhou and Haven-1 remain undated
desks.summary: Starship Flight 15 (13 Nov) reached orbit and deployed Starlink satellites; the ship was then caught by the tower (reported by several outlets), but the booster catch was called off and the booster was lost in the Gulf of Mexico.

top_stories.title: Starship Flight 15: ship reaches orbit, booster catch aborted
top_stories.why_it_matters: A 22-hour test with a ship catch is a step toward reuse, but the booster missed its tower catch, so rapid double reuse is still unproven.

top_stories.title: Flight 15 recap: Starlink deployment and booster catch outcome
top_stories.why_it_matters: Confirms the flight carried Starlink deployment objectives, tying Starship's economics to satellite launch while lunar refuelling awaits demonstration.

top_stories.title: Vast Haven-1 private station slips to no earlier than Q1 2027
top_stories.why_it_matters: The first commercial station, a stepping stone to a post-ISS presence, is later than planned; crew flights also depend on SpaceX docking safety sign-off.

top_stories.title: China's Long March 10A booster flew a Mengzhou abort test with sea splashdown
top_stories.why_it_matters: Shows China rehearsing a reusable lunar-class booster and crew escape ahead of its 2030 crewed landing goal; one grid fin may not have fully deployed.

top_stories.title: Mengzhou 1 and Long March 10A prepare for first flight
top_stories.why_it_matters: Marks the planned orbital debut of China's crew capsule; this sweep found no evidence it has flown yet.

top_stories.title: Space weather quiet on 14 Nov: low activity, eight sunspot regions
top_stories.why_it_matters: Solar cycle 25 is past peak but still active; quiet conditions pose no near-term threat to satellites or crewed flights.

trajectory.six_months: Expect investigation of the booster abort, a Flight 16, possibly the first propellant transfer demonstration, and a Mengzhou 1 attempt.
trajectory.two_years: Artemis III orbital rehearsal in 2027 and a landing attempt around Artemis IV in 2028 are the milestones; a persistent crewed base is still beyond this window.

desks.name: Natural Hazards & Wildcards
desks.midnight_definition: A natural or out-of-the-blue event (supervolcanic eruption, impactor, extreme solar storm, mega-quake) with global consequences that nobody was positioned for.
desks.headline: Banda Sea quake and minor solar storm: regional hazards only, no global-scale threat
desks.summary: Hazard activity is elevated but regional: a large Banda Sea quake on 16 November (magnitude 6.6 on the USGS listing, 7.1 in other reports), a minor geomagnetic storm watch (Kp forecast up to about 4.7) for 17-18 November from a coronal hole plus a glancing CME, and ongoing Kilauea eruptive episodes. Campi Flegrei remains at the yellow alert level per INGV.

top_stories.title: Banda Sea quake off Tual, Indonesia, rated M6.6 by USGS with Green alert
top_stories.why_it_matters: A large intermediate-depth event; USGS Green alert implies low expected casualties. Other outlets report a 7.1 upgrade and conflicting depths, and no damage or casualties were confirmed in the reports I saw.

top_stories.title: Near-G1 geomagnetic storm watch for 17-18 Nov (Kp forecast up to 4.67) after a fast CME and coronal-hole stream
top_stories.why_it_matters: NOAA forecast Kp up to 4.67; a CME leaving the Sun on 14 Nov gave only a low-confidence glancing blow. Expected impacts are weak grid fluctuations and minor satellite effects, activity easing by 19 Nov.

top_stories.title: Asteroid 2026 WA reported to pass Earth at about 126,400 km
top_stories.why_it_matters: One outlet reports a harmless close pass at roughly a third of the Moon's distance, found in advance; the fact-checker could not confirm the figure.

top_stories.title: Kilauea north vent fountains lava about 200 m for six hours; next episode forecast 16-21 Nov
top_stories.why_it_matters: Episodic eruption in Hawaii with a predictable cycle; local hazard (ash, gas), no global effect.

top_stories.title: Strong shallow M6.4 quake hits Santa Cruz Islands, Solomon Islands
top_stories.why_it_matters: Shallow event with a USGS Green alert; regional, routine for the Ring of Fire.

top_stories.title: Campi Flegrei M4.7 quake injures 21 and damages buildings near Naples (carried)
top_stories.why_it_matters: The strongest shock of the current unrest hurt 21 people and closed Pozzuoli port; shows real local damage potential.

trajectory.six_months: Expect continued Campi Flegrei quakes with a real chance of further M4+ events, routine global M6-7 quakes, repeating Kilauea episodes, and recurring G1-G2 storms as the solar cycle declines.
trajectory.two_years: Solar flare intensity should fall but extreme storms stay possible; Campi Flegrei unrest could plateau or escalate; Iceland's Reykjanes system is likely to erupt again with regional effect.
